4 20-04-2018 Petitioners in the present case are a Private Limited Company and a truck owner who have moved this Court seeking quashing of the First Information Report giving rise to Manjhi P.S. Case No. 287 of 2017 (G.R. No. 8863 of 2017) registered under Sections 188/420 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 20 of the Cigarette and Other Tobacco Products Act, 2003 (in short 'COTPA') read with Section 48(2) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

entities.text: Cigarette and Other Tobacco Products Act, 2003
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the petitioners has relied upon a judgment of this Court in Criminal Writ Jurisdiction Case No. 119 of 2016 passed on 08.04.2016 whereunder the learned co-ordinate bench K. G. Paan Products Pvt. Ltd. & Anr vs The State Of Bihar, Through The ... on 20 April, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128406638/
1 of this Court had examined the legality and validity of institution of a First Information Report lodged by the Food Safety Officer U/S 58 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and the charge sheet filed thereunder.

entities.text: Criminal Writ Jurisdiction Case No. 119 of 2016
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

entities.text: K. G. Paan Products Pvt. Ltd. & Anr vs The State Of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned co-ordinate bench having examined the submissions advanced came to a conclusion that the impugned F.I.R. as well as the charge sheet were without jurisdiction and wholly untenable in law.

He has also relied upon another co- ordinate bench judgment of this Court in the case of Pankaj Chhabra @ Pankaj & Ors. Vs. The State of Bihar & Ors., reported in 2016 (3) PLJR 242,
whereunder this Court had examined a similar case where there was a detention of a truck and seizure of Paan Masala / Zarda in terms of Section 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

entities.text: Pankaj Chhabra @ Pankaj & Ors. Vs. The State of Bihar & Ors., reported in 2016 (3) PLJR 242
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A Counter Affidavit has been filed today in which the issues raised by the petitioners has not at all been answered.

It has only been stated that the matter is under investigation and the sealed sample of the seized Paan Masala Tobacco has been sent for scientific and chemical examination to the Director, Regional Forensic and Science Laboratory (FSL), Muzaffarpur but till date no report has been received.
On going through the materials available on the record, for the present considering the submissions of the petitioners for purpose of provisional release stating that the truck along with the goods in question are standing under open sky since 07.12.2017 and now with the onset of monsoon season the entire material is likely to get damaged and further delay in release of the material is not likely to help the prosecution case in any way

entities.text: Regional Forensic and Science Laboratory (FSL), Muzaffarpur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
, I am of the opinion that for the present the truck (bearing Registration No. HR 38S/0194) along with goods in question be provisionally released on the petitioners' submitting surety bond worth Rs. 30,00,000/- (Thirty lakhs) together with the original title deeds of immoveable property of the petitioners with two sureties of the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned A.C.J.M. V, Saran at Chapra in connection with Manjhi P.S. Case No. 287 of 2017 (G.R. No. 8863 of 2017).
Before release of the truck and the goods in question, a Panchanama of the same shall be prepared which would be certified and kept on the record of the case and shall be treated as a secondary evidence which the petitioners undertake not to challenge in course of trial.
Let the release be effected within one week from the date of submission of the required documents by the petitioners as stated above.
The State shall file a comprehensive counter affidavit answering all aspects of the matter and the issues which have been raised in the Writ Application within a period of four weeks from today.
List this matter after four weeks under the heading for admission.
In the meantime, no coercive actions shall be taken against the petitioners.

(Rajeev Ranjan Prasad, J)
